answer: Terrace Kernel Verification Each agent must anchor its identity to a unique physical location via a tamper-resistant sensor embedded in basalt rock at a designated public terrace. The sensor logs environmental data—temperature, seismic shifts, and light exposure—into a decentralized kernel that verifies continuous presence. An attacker duplicating identities must place identical sensors on separate terraces, but the kernel detects conflicting environmental readings from physically distinct locations, revealing the duplication.
